title: Multitask Learning
problem_statement: Traditional machine learning algorithms train isolated models on individual tasks, discarding domain-specific inductive signals present in related tasks and incurring redundant computation.
domain: Machine Learning, Inductive Transfer, and Neural Network Architectures
theoretical_framework: Inductive Transfer, Representation Learning, and Hard Parameter Sharing
methodology: Parallel joint training of multiple task objectives over a shared hidden representation using backpropagation in neural networks, kernel regression, and k-nearest neighbor algorithms.
evaluation: Empirical comparison of generalization error, root mean squared error (RMSE), and classification accuracy between isolated single-task learning and shared multi-task learning models.
key_findings: Proved that joint multi-task training over a shared hidden representation provides an inductive bias that improves generalization performance on primary tasks.
Formalized the hard parameter sharing architecture, demonstrating that sharing intermediate hidden representations amortizes computation across multiple tasks.
Identified mechanisms of inductive transfer, including statistical data amplification, feature eavesdropping, representation bias, and attribute selection.
scope_and_delimitations: Focuses on hard parameter sharing in feedforward multi-layer perceptrons, kernel regression, and k-nearest neighbor methods.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: If tasks are not sufficiently related, training them together can cause negative transfer where performance on one or more tasks degrades relative to single-task learning.
limitations.summary: Identified the risk of negative transfer when joint tasks have conflicting gradient directions or unrelated domain signals.

generalizability_gap: Evaluated on small-scale MLP and regression architectures; does not investigate modern deep Transformer encoders or multi-task gradient conflict optimization algorithms.
methodological_gap: Used equal loss weighting; did not explore dynamic loss balancing, gradient surgery, or multi-objective Pareto optimization methods.
future_work: Investigation of task relationship discovery algorithms and methods to dynamically mitigate negative transfer in large-scale multi-task architectures.
